1fa04992eb6cc1d917b30a96af486f03b4de266f.name: compact.ua
1fa04992eb6cc1d917b30a96af486f03b4de266f.code:
N ← ↥6 ⋕◇∘⊡1 &args
~Tree {Id Left Right}
Leaf   ← Tree ⊃(⊣|⋅[]|⋅[])
Build  ← |1 ⨬(Tree ⊃(⊣|Build ⊃[-1⊢|×2⊣]|Build ⊃[-1⊢|+1×2⊣])|Leaf) ⊸(=0⊢)
Check  ← |1 ⨬(+1+⊃(Check Tree.Left)(Check Tree.Right)|⋅1) ⊸(=0⧻Tree.Left)
TreeAt ← Build ⊟⊙1
&p $"stretch tree of depth _\t check: _" ⟜(Check TreeAt) +1N
Long       ← TreeAt N
Depths     ← +4×2⇡+1⌊÷2 -4N
Iteration  ← +⊃(Check TreeAt)(⋅∘)
Iterations ← ˜ⁿ2-⊙(+4N)
SumChecks  ← ∧Iteration ⊃(↯⊃Iterations∘|⋅0)
Batch      ← &p $"_\t trees of depth _\t check: _" ⊃(Iterations|∘|SumChecks)
≡Batch Depths
&p $"long lived tree of depth _\t check: _" N Check Long

binarytrees.method: Pinned runtime source proof; no substitute tree kernel or benchmark instrumentation.
binarytrees.proof_scope: Each constructor produces a new nonempty three-element boxed-node buffer. Child trees are recursively constructed by separate calls and then referenced from parent boxes. Allocator addresses may be reused after a short-lived tree is freed; they cannot be shared by simultaneously live node buffers. Empty leaf child sentinels may be shared, while each leaf node buffer is fresh.

proof.excerpt:
N ← ↥6 ⋕◇∘⊡1 &args
~Tree {Id Left Right}
Leaf   ← Tree ⊃(⊣|⋅[]|⋅[])
Build  ← |1 ⨬(Tree ⊃(⊣|Build ⊃[-1⊢|×2⊣]|Build ⊃[-1⊢|+1×2⊣])|Leaf) ⊸(=0⊢)
Check  ← |1 ⨬(+1+⊃(Check Tree.Left)(Check Tree.Right)|⋅1) ⊸(=0⧻Tree.Left)
TreeAt ← Build ⊟⊙1
&p $"stretch tree of depth _\t check: _" ⟜(Check TreeAt) +1N
Long       ← TreeAt N
Depths     ← +4×2⇡+1⌊÷2 -4N
Iteration  ← +⊃(Check TreeAt)(⋅∘)
Iterations ← ˜ⁿ2-⊙(+4N)
SumChecks  ← ∧Iteration ⊃(↯⊃Iterations∘|⋅0)
Batch      ← &p $"_\t trees of depth _\t check: _" ⊃(Iterations|∘|SumChecks)
≡Batch Depths
&p $"long lived tree of depth _\t check: _" N Check Long
proof.conclusion: Build makes two independent recursive calls, each at depth-1; Leaf also calls Tree. Long is constructed before all short-lived batches and traversed afterward. Iteration calls Check TreeAt anew for every element of the requested iteration vector; no tree or check formula is substituted.
The three-field boxed Tree data constructor is a callable Node::Array, with one field argument for each of Id, Left and Right.
Every runtime constructor invocation drains its field values and creates fresh scalar boxes, then assembles the fields into an array.
Each scalar box is a fresh one-element cowslice, not an interned or memoized node.
A boxed array starts with the first freshly created scalar box.
The freshly created first box buffer reserves capacity for all three fields before fields are appended.
The other boxed fields are appended to that new buffer; the node is a three-element Array<Boxed>.
cowslice! constructs an ecow vector; node data are reference-counted buffers.
A nonempty ecow buffer allocates storage through grow, beginning with a fresh empty vector.
grow on a new vector invokes alloc::alloc::alloc with a nonzero layout, proving separate simultaneously live backing allocations.
The evaluated Long tree is stored in the global binding table as an owned constant; later short-lived iterations cannot release this reference.
Reading Long clones its stored value without replacing or dropping the original global binding.
Cloning buffers retains references; buffers are released only when the final reference is dropped. Long and its child buffers remain live through all batches.
Compiler pre-evaluation requires bounded pure expressions. Tree depth comes from runtime args; recursive Build remains a function invoked for each requested tree.
A second visit to a recursive function fails the purity walk, so normal compiler pre-evaluation cannot turn Build into a cached constructed subtree.

binarytrees.limitation: No runtime address trace was collected. The distinct-node and retention findings follow the exact pinned constructor, allocation and ownership implementations.

native_runtime_proof.conclusion: Modifiers consume their recursive strand operand. Unparenthesized nested Rows here binds only Fix; Norm already binds nested Rows to Reduce Add and leaves Self Mul on the whole array.
Fix is a recognized general monadic native array function, applying fix_depth at the requested depth.
Nested Rows over a recognized function increments its depth instead of executing a user function for each row.
Rows dispatches recognized native functions once over the array; unmatched composite functions use the row-by-row env.exec fallback.
General depth-aware Fix changes the shape; the benchmark matrix has no map-key metadata.
fix_depth inserts a singleton dimension at the requested depth, without copying numeric data.
